body_markdown:
Chevrolet truck engineers have been busy lately. The General’s most popular and profitable product line is getting a major revamp for 2027, with the Silverado 1500 showing off a new look inside and out. Under the skin, the chassis will be familiar, but the front suspension has been updated with new upper mounts. The biggest news is the truck’s powertrains, with two Gen-VI gasoline V-8s, an improved 2.7-liter Turbomax four-cylinder shoring up the base, and the 3.0-liter Duramax inline-six returning as the only diesel option in full-size, light-duty trucks on the market. We’ll cover the Heavy Duty models and their improved 6.6-liter gasoline V-8 and 550-hp, 8.3-liter Duramax diesel next week. For now, let’s focus on the Bow Tie brand’s bread and butter, the Silverado 1500.


## Exterior


From a design perspective, the 2027 Chevrolet Silverado is an evolution of the previous truck’s styling. New exterior sheet metal brings pronounced shoulders to the fenders and bedsides. Larger headlights bookend new grilles, but the look is familiar thanks to consistent Bow Tie placement. The greenhouse is also similar, but the rear side windows are more squared off. Overall, the trucks are handsome and perhaps a bit understated, but Chevy added a hint of flair with new bedside emblems and more details in the lighting elements. Overall, it’s an improvement on what was already a well-received design.


DW Burnett


DW Burnett


## Interior


While the 2027 Silverado 1500 has an all-new interior, Chevrolet’s drive event included the 2027 Heavy Duty models, which carry over the interior design from the 2026 models. That meant we got to see old and new side by side. The difference isn’t jarring, at least in the top trim models. Drawing inspiration from the Silverado EV’s dash, the center screens in all 1500 trims come in at 16.3 inches (in the previous generation, lower trims had a different dash design than upper trims). Also like the Silverado EV, the center screens virtually blend into the driver information screen behind the wheel. Chevy’s infotainment system features Google Built-In, which utilizes Google Maps, Google Play, and Gemini AI, all available without being connected to a phone. If you’re more familiar with CarPlay or Android Auto, all models come with wireless capability for both of those as well. With all trim levels using a similar center stack, the biggest differentiation in the dash comes in High Country and ZR2, which both feature an 11.5-inch passenger-side screen that can be used for displaying streaming video.


Chevrolet


Chevrolet


DW Burnett


A new steering wheel includes shift paddles along with four additional buttons on the back for navigating the audio system. There’s also a traditional volume knob and a row of buttons flanked by HVAC knobs for the dual-zone climate control, allowing the most-used features to be front and center. Chevrolet did a good job of making the touchscreen intuitive and keeping things from getting buried in sub-menus. Still, those who aren’t fans of touchscreens will have no other options for accessing functions like the seat heaters and ventilation.


Chevrolet


Chevrolet


## Powertrains


Chevrolet remains the only manufacturer offering a half-ton diesel option. The power-dense and fuel-sipping 3.0-liter Duramax returns in the 2027 Silverado with the same 305 horsepower and 495 lb.-ft. of torque that pulls a ½-ton truck with ease. Demand for the Duramax will, naturally, depend on the price of diesel. If prices return to only a slight premium over gas, we’d expect this to be a popular choice.


The turbocharged, 2.7-liter four-cylinder Turbomax engine returns as the base engine for the Silverado in WT, Custom, Custom Trail Boss, Z71, and LT trims, but it has some big improvements. A new turbocharger increases the airflow and uses its dual-volute design to carry its flat torque plateau higher up the powerband. It brings a new fuel pump along with it, injecting fuel at even higher pressure. The result is 455 lb.-ft. of torque, up 25 lb.-ft., along with an increase of 40 horsepower, bringing the total to 350. The previous iteration already felt like a solid alternative to port-injected versions of the venerable 5.3-liter V-8, not to mention the 4.3-liter V-6 it was meant to replace. The other big news for the base powerplant is that it’s now paired with the 10-speed automatic, ditching the eight-speed that it used previously. We didn’t drive any 2.7-liter models at Chevrolet’s Tucson, Arizona, launch event, as Chevy was focused on introducing its two new V-8s.


[Brandan Gillogly](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/brandan-gillogly/)


As we[initially shared about a year ago](https://www.hagerty.com/media/news/report-gms-new-small-block-v-8-due-in-dual-displacements/) , the long-running 5.3-liter and 6.2-liter V-8s are making way for a 5.7 and a 6.6. With 2027 representing the 60th anniversary of the 350, Chevy thought the most recognized small-block displacement from the engine’s first two generations should make a comeback. To get that familiar displacement, Chevy kept the 3.78-inch bore of the 5.3-liter and added .236 to the stroke for a total of 3.854 inches. That makes the 5.7-liter the first undersquare small-block ever, which helps it achieve its impressive 428 lb.-ft. of torque along with 402 hp.


With the 5.7-liter encroaching on the power output of the previous Silverado’s 6.2, Chevrolet paired a crank that yielded a 3.854-inch stroke with its 4.065-inch bore to increase displacement to 6.6 liters. The bigger V-8 uses a unique intake manifold. Thanks to its higher displacement, torque comes more easily, so engineers could afford to use larger, shorter runners that shift the torque curve higher in the rpm range. This big-inch small-block will be available in the ZR2 and High Country 4×4, where it produces 481 hp and 501 lb.-ft. of torque.


Mike Kobica, one of the small-block’s engineers, gave us a basic overview of the new engines. The 4.4-inch bore spacing is the same, naturally, and some of the gaskets and seals carry over, but that’s about it. “There’s not a lot of commonalities between our Gen 5 and Gen 6,” Kubica said. “It’s all new stuff. New block, new heads, new crank, new cams, new intakes. . .”


The blocks on both 1500 V-8s are cast aluminum with cast iron liners. In a switch from previous Gen III, IV, and V-8s, the Gen VI engines use a slightly taller deck height. We didn’t get the exact dimension, but were told it’s about a quarter of an inch taller, which seems to coincide with the .235-inch increase in stroke. The change in deck height means that intakes won’t interchange between Gen VI engines and earlier versions.


There are a couple of quick ways to discern a Gen VI 350 from a 400. The easiest option may be a bit obscured when the engine is installed, but both blocks are cast with their cubic inch displacements on the front driver side, by cylinder number 1. The other telltale is the size of the throttle body, which is eight millimeters larger in diameter on the 6.6.


[Brandan Gillogly](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/brandan-gillogly/)


All Gen VI V-8 engines use dual fuel injection. Like the Gen V engines, direct fuel injectors are located in the cylinder head below the intake ports. The new port injectors are also in the cylinder head, unlike the intake manifold on the last port-injected GM V-8s. Dual fueling lets the engine idle on port injection for quieter operation, and spraying fuel on the back of the intake valves helps reduce carbon buildup from crankcase vapors. Depending on the demands on the engine, fuel can come from either set of injectors, or both.


Below the rectangular fuel rail is the fuel injector that runs through the valve cover and into the intake port.


[Brandan Gillogly](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/brandan-gillogly/)


A new cooling system for the Gen VI engine includes new coolant routing in the cylinder heads, a welcome upgrade given their 13:1 compression ratio. The system also now divides the cooling circuit for the transmission fluid and engine oil, which were previously cooled to the same temperature. The new, divided system **** allows both fluids to heat up quickly and help efficiency while keeping the transmission happily churning at a cooler temperature even when towing heavy loads. Enough for the tech talk, let’s find out how they perform.


## On the Road


It should come as no surprise that a pushrod V-8 with more torque and horsepower is an improvement over its predecessor. With a few thousand pounds of camping trailer hitched behind the Silverado, the 5.7 pulled easily. Chevy’s Transparent Trailer camera system helps eliminate blind spots and makes it much easier to know when it’s safe to merge into traffic. The increased displacement from the new V-8 makes itself known with a broad torque curve. It’s smooth, quiet, and easily gets the job done. The 5.7 just feels like a burlier version of the hardworking 5.3 it replaced.


DW Burnett


## **Specs: 2027 Chevrolet Silverado 1500 Z71** ****


**Price:** $56,995/$60,180 (base Z71/as-tested)
**Powertrain** : 5.7-liter pushrod V-8, ten-speed automatic transmission
**Horsepower:** 402
**Torque:** 428 lb-ft
**Layout:** Four-wheel-drive, four-door, five-passenger pickup
**Weight:** 5,060 lbs.
**EPA-rated fuel economy:** Not yet available
**Competitors:**[Ford F-150](https://www.hagerty.com/media/tags/ford-f-150/) ,[Ram 1500](https://www.hagerty.com/media/tags/ram-1500/)


The 6.6, meanwhile, feels like a muscle car engine. It’s still a small-block, but it has big-block displacement and the big-block power and torque that go with it. It even sounds the part, at least a little bit. At idle, the bigger V-8 has a subtle rumble that’s noticeable from outside the cab. Under light throttle, it behaves itself. There’s enough torque on tap to get through normal driving with a light touch on the pedal. Get just a bit aggressive, however, and the 6.6 changes its tone with a guttural rumble. This is the right engine for the ZR2.


## Off-Road


Just as before, the ZR2 balances impressive off-road capability with fantastic on-road manners. The DSSV dampers provide fantastic ride and handling on pavement. Because they don’t rely on any kind of outside sensors or electronics, the shocks handle the transition from roads to rough dirt without any driver input.


In addition to the powertrain and interior upgrades that come to all 2027 Silverado models, the 2027 ZR2 adds more capability. Jounce bumpers and 35-inch tires were both previously only available with the ZR2 Bison option package. Now they’re standard on the ZR2. The AEV Bison package will add even more skid plates as well as steel bumpers front and rear. For those who don’t want to step up to the ultimate Silverado off-roader, the Trail Boss also gets improved off-road hardware, including 34-inch rubber.


DW Burnett


Baja Mode returns for higher-speed off-road action in the sand and dirt, where the ZR2 is in its element. Whether it’s the standard Duramax inline-six or the big V-8, Baja Mode offers reprogrammed shifts from the 10-speed that keep the engine revved up and ready to apply power to maintain momentum. Baja Mode also allows plenty of latitude to kick the rear end out around turns without traction control reining things in.


To highlight the ZR2’s low-speed performance, Chevy engineers tuned the ZR2’s Off Road mode to help drivers crawl over rocks and ledges with more confidence. We scrambled over a rock-strewn trail with the transfer case in low range, trying the ZR2’s Off Road mode in Drive as well as L2 and L1. All three modes dampen the throttle response for more precision, and each one applies progressively stronger braking when lifting off the throttle. Using L1 allows for one-pedal driving at low speeds and wasn’t immediately intuitive. It took a few minutes to realize that the throttle was necessary even when descending.


[Brandan Gillogly](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/brandan-gillogly/)


[Brandan Gillogly](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/brandan-gillogly/)


Underbody skid plates and the side steps that serve as rocker guards each came in handy when dropping down ledges. The ZR2’s under-body and side-mounted cameras were also quite useful off-road. They’re no replacement for a spotter or an experienced driver, but they certainly make things a lot easier and help place tires on the right obstacles.


DW Burnett


There are still a staggering number of build configurations available for the 2027 Silverado 1500. Our brief drives barely scratched the surface. What Chevrolet has shown so far seems to only improve an already impressive truck and provide buyers with more of what they’re looking for as far as comfort, convenience, towing performance, and off-road capability. GM wants to maintain its sales lead in the pickup market and seems to have a strong lineup to hit the heart of the market.


## **2027 Chevrolet Silverado 1500** ****


**Highs:** Comfortable interior; plenty of powertrain choices; improved off-road capability for Trail Boss and ZR2; Trillium Green Metallic paint is stunning.


**Lows:** Chevy still has a gap in the lineup with no competitor for the high-power Ram TRX and F-150 Raptor R.


**Takeaway:** The new V-8s have a lot riding on them, but the return of the 350 and 400 isn’t just nostalgia.
